Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1137 AM CDT Sat Jul 25 2026

Valid 251630Z - 261200Z

...THERE IS AN ENHANCED RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR CENTRAL
INTO EASTERN SOUTH DAKOTA...

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS IN CENTRAL AND
EASTERN MONTANA...

...SUMMARY...
Widespread severe gusts are possible across South Dakota late this
afternoon through the evening.

...SD into adjacent parts of IA/MN...
A prominent upper ridge centered over the central/southern Rockies
will feature the southern periphery of appreciably strong mid to
high-level flow extending from the Pacific Northwest across the
northern High Plains and into the north-central states.  Late
morning surface analysis shows very hot temperatures ensuing across
western NE into the western half of SD with richer moisture (surface
dewpoints in the lower to mid 70s F) located over the eastern half
of NE/SD.  Visible-satellite imagery shows some mid to high clouds
across northern WY moving towards the Black Hills.  This patch of
clouds appears associated with a weak disturbance forecast to move
into western SD later this afternoon.  

Downstream across SD, forecast soundings show very steep surface to
500-mb lapse rates developing as temperatures rise into the 100s F. 
Expecting initially isolated to widely scattered storms to develop
near the Black Hills, as convective temperatures are breached. 
Models show the gradual development of a cluster moving east across
SD early this evening.  Have increased severe-wind probabilities to
account for observational and model-based trends towards an MCS
capable of peak gusts in the 75-90 mph range.  This activity will
probably slowly weaken towards the MN/IA/SD border but perhaps
continue into early overnight with a wind threat.  

...MT...
Isolated to scattered storms will likely form near the higher
terrain of southern MT later this afternoon with a gradual increase
in storm coverage as this moves east during the early evening.  A
hot and well-mixed boundary layer will support severe gusts with the
stronger cores and associated outflow.  There is some indication
this activity will cluster and potentially reach parts of
eastern/southeast MT by the late evening.  

...Upper Midwest/Upper Great Lakes...
Conditional severe potential exists across parts of the Upper
Midwest spanning Minnesota to Upper Michigan into Wisconsin.  Models
continue to show low storm chances as mid-level heights rise through
the late evening.  Nonetheless, appreciable heating of a seasonably
moist boundary layer will result in strong potential buoyancy later
today into tonight.  Elongated hodographs will support organized
storms capable of a wind/hail threat.  Given a muted diurnal storm
signal in models, the greater chance for isolated storms appears to
be associated with warm advection activity late tonight.  

...Northeast NV/northern UT/eastern ID...
Storm development is expected during the afternoon across parts of
northeast Nevada, along the western periphery of the upper ridge. 
These storms will spread into adjacent parts of southeast Idaho and
northwest Utah with time.  Isolated severe gusts may accompany the
stronger downdrafts.  

...South-central/southeast AZ...
High-based convection is again expected across southeast Arizona
during the afternoon, with initial downburst potential.  A modest
enhancement to easterly flow along the southern periphery of the
upper ridge may allow for localized strong to severe wind gusts to
spread westward into parts of south-central Arizona, before
convection weakens tonight.

..Smith/Moore.. 07/25/2026

$$

Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1219 PM CDT Sat Jul 25 2026

Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE MID
MISSOURI VALLEY ACROSS THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY AND WESTERN
GREAT LAKES...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms capable of large hail and damaging winds are
possible from the upper Mississippi Valley and Great Lakes into
portions of the mid Missouri Valley on Sunday and Sunday night.

...From eastern SD and NE to the Upper Great Lakes...
The forecast continues to have major uncertainties regarding
placement of the most likely severe storm corridors, with a wide
range of model solutions. In general, the most likely threat areas
include northern MN into WI and Upper MI, on the periphery of the
upper ridge and where stronger winds aloft will exist coincident
with strong instability, and from southeast SD into northeast NE
within a super-heated surface trough.

Beneath 40-50 kt midlevel northwesterlies, areas of strong
instability will develop with relatively steep midlevel lapse rates
and 70s F dewpoints, from parts of MN into WI. Models suggest
various storm clusters are possible late in the day, and these would
travel quickly southeastward with damaging wind and hail likely.
Some severe activity could potentially push south of the Slight Risk
area into more of northern IL, IN, and Lower MI. However, the
instability gradient will be a limiting factor for eastward extent.

Clusters of storms, possibly forming into a small MCS, are also
expected where very hot temperatures develop into SD. The deeply
mixed boundary layer combined with surface convergence within the
low pressure trough will support afternoon development over eastern
SD, with a corridor of damaging wind potential extending
southeastward into eastern NE and western IA. 

...SC and GA...
Daytime heating of a high PWAT air mass will lead to moderate
instability during the afternoon. A surface trough will deepen over
the central Carolinas and into eastern GA, with an uncapped air mass
and weak convergence yielding scattered storms. Shear will be weak,
but modest northwest flow aloft should support corridors of damaging
wind gusts as storms develop southeastward toward the coast.

..Jewell.. 07/25/2026

$$

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0219 AM CDT Sat Jul 25 2026

Valid 271200Z - 281200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER THE GREAT
LAKES INTO PARTS OF THE OHIO VALLEY...

...SUMMARY...
Severe storms capable of damaging winds and large hail are possible
across the Great Lakes into the Ohio Valley Monday into Monday
night.

...Synopsis...
A potent short-wave trough and associated 50+ kt mid-level jet will
move through the Great Lakes within the northeast periphery of an
upper high centered over the southern High Plains. That upper-air
system will be attended by a deepening surface low that is forecast
to develop from the MN Arrowhead through the U.P. and northern Lower
MI into southwest ON during the forecast period. Meanwhile, a
trailing cold front will advance through the upper Midwest and Great
Lakes into the OH Valley.


...Great Lakes and Ohio Valley...
Clusters of thunderstorms may be ongoing Monday morning across parts
of the Midwest and upper Great Lakes within a broad zone of
low-level warm advection and increasing forcing/DCVA downstream from
the mid-level trough. A fairly large area of moderate instability
and seasonably strong vertical shear is forecast at the outset of
the forecast period, and as such, the most intense storms will be
capable of large hail and damaging winds. A subset of the early-day
storms may evolve into one or multiple MCSs by afternoon ahead of
the surface low and cold front, leading to a corridor of more
focused damaging wind potential from Lower MI into IN and OH, and
possibly parts of KY and WV Monday night.

Despite the presence of strong instability along the front from the
mid MS Valley into mid/lower MO Valley, stronger capping and weaker
forcing for ascent are expected to lower the chance of thunderstorm
development.


...Central High Plains...
Thunderstorms are expected to develop Monday afternoon into evening
within a moderately unstable, post-frontal upslope flow regime.
Generally weak vertical shear is expected to limit storm
organization; however, the presence of steep low/mid-level lapse
rates and potentially large temperature-dewpoint spreads suggests a
threat for isolated severe wind gusts.

..Mead.. 07/25/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0345 AM CDT Sat Jul 25 2026

Valid 281200Z - 021200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Tuesday...
An upper low is forecast to develop from southwest ON into the
northern Mid-Atlantic with an attending belt of 35-45 kt mid-level
flow extending from the OH Valley into the southern Mid-Atlantic. 
At the surface, a cyclone will remain vertically aligned with the
upper low, while a trailing cold front advances through the upper OH
and TN Valleys into the Mid-Atlantic, Carolinas, and Gulf Coast
states. A lee trough is expected to develop ahead of the cold front
along the Piedmont Tuesday afternoon.
 
Showers and thunderstorms (some potentially strong) are expected to
be ongoing Tuesday morning from the upper OH Valley into the
Mid-Atlantic, aided by forcing for ascent ahead of the upper low and
low-level warm air and moisture advection along a 30-40 kt low-level
jet. That activity is expected to linger into the afternoon from NY
and PA into western New England, which will limit the potential for
air mass destabilization in those areas. Stronger daytime heating
appears possible south of the Mason-Dixon Line, where moderate
instability is forecast across the pre-frontal warm sector. 

Thunderstorms are expected to increase in coverage and intensity
during the afternoon along the cold front and lee trough from the
Delmarva into central Appalachians and VA/NC Piedmont. The moderate
instability combined with 35-40 kt of deep-layer shear will support
organized storm modes with the primary hazard being damaging wind
gusts.

Other more isolated severe storms appear possible over the central
High Plains within a low-level upslope regime.  

  
...Day 5/Wednesday...
The Day 4/Tuesday upper low is forecast to slowly drift northeast
with a belt of stronger mid-level winds overspreading New England. A
surface low will remain vertically aligned with the mid-level system
with convergence in the vicinity of that feature and a trailing
front serving as the focus for afternoon thunderstorm development.
The models suggest that southern to central parts of New England may
become moderately unstable, which, combined with the slight shear
enhancement, may support a few strong to severe storms.

Additional strong to severe storms appear possible along a frontal
zone in the Southeast, where a very moist air mass will contribute
to moderate to strong instability.

Uncertainty in the extent of the severe weather threat in both areas
precludes the delineation of a 15% probability contour.  


...Days 6-8/Thursday through Saturday...

The 00Z ensemble means are in reasonably good agreement in depicting
the retrogression of the upper high from the Southern Rockies into
the lower CO Valley. A concurrent weakening and broadening of the
eastern CONUS trough is also forecast. There is a model signal for a
stronger mid-level system to move into BC and the Pacific Northwest
by Day 8/Saturday. Deterministic guidance indicates a series of weak
disturbances tracking from the northern Plains to along and east of
the MS Valley during this time period with sporadic occurrences of
severe weather possible. However, the large-scale pattern currently
appears unsupportive of an organized severe weather episode.

..Mead.. 07/25/2026
